messages:
Maya K.: hey team — i'm taking primary for the next 8h. quick handoff: there's an ongoing pager for increased token latency to the hosted API (pager fired ~20m ago). i'm attaching the quick checklist i ran and what i think the immediate next steps are. :wave:

Jamal R.: thanks Maya. do we have customer impact? any errors surfaced or just latency?

Maya K.: IncidentBot summary: 3.2% p95 latency regression on text-generation across us-west-2. error rates are normal. most traffic is slowed, customers seeing slower completions. some SSO partners reported timeouts at 10s.

IncidentBot: [AUTO] Pager triggered: latency-regression-us-west-2 (sev:2). links: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1958887777, runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/latency-regression

Evan S.: copying runbook steps i use for this one: 1) confirm KV cache hit rate 2) check gpu host saturation 3) validate recent deployments to model-serving 4) fallback routing if saturation high.

Maya K.: exact quick commands i ran: 
```
# KV cache hit rate
curl -sS https://metrics.internal/api/query?m=kv_cache_hit_rate | jq
# host saturation (top p95 gpu util)
kubectl -n inference exec -it pod/gpu-metrics -- /bin/sh -c "cat /proc/gpu_stats"
```
results: KV cache hit rate dropped ~15% in last 30m on model v1.3.2. GPU util across pool is 68% but with spike tails at 95% on 2 nodes.

Priya D.: dropping hit rate could be due to recent rollout of v1.3.2? we did a canary at 00:10 UTC. who rolled that out?

Maya K.: rollout author is @Evan S. (confirmed in deploy log). Evan, can you paste the deploy sha/notes?

Evan S.: yep, deploy 7a2c9f rolled at 00:12. changes: kv-prefetch tuning and small tokenization tweak. logs show no obvious exceptions but prefetch window got smaller (by design).

Jamal R.: that would explain hit-rate drop. mitigation options: 1) increase prefetch window on v1.3.2 config (fast) 2) rollback to v1.3.1 (slower, more impact) 3) enable cross-region fallback for a subset of traffic (immediate but increases cost).

Maya K.: plan for now: (A) increase prefetch to previous value on an emergency config patch to v1.3.2 (low blast) (B) enable fallback routing for 10% of high-latency requests to model v1.2.x in us-west-2 policy (temporary) (C) monitor p95 and SSO timeouts.

SRE Bot: template patch for emergency config: https://redwood.internal/configs/kv-prefetch/emergency-patch. Use `rwdctl apply --patch emergency-patch` and watch rollout with `rwdctl rollout status`.

Maya K.: i'll apply the patch now and watch. tagging @Priya D. to be on secondary for 15m in case i need escalation. Priya — you ok to be second?

Priya D.: on it. i'll be available. please ping if latency persists after 10m.

(2m later)

Maya K.: applied emergency patch `kv-prefetch +20%` to v1.3.2 on the inference pool. rollout completed to 80% in 90s, 100% in 3m.

IncidentBot: [UPDATE] config-patch-applied by Maya K. — monitoring metrics.

Evan S.: i'm enabling fallback routing for 10% of traffic to v1.2.x now. command: `rwdctl routing apply --policy fallback10pct-usw2`.

Maya K.: monitoring dashboard: p95 trending down from 3.2s -> 1.4s over 6m, SSO timeouts dropped to 0.2% from 1.8%. KV cache hit rate recovering to within 5% of baseline.

Jamal R.: nice. keep an eye on GPU tail nodes — might still see occasional spikes. if spikes > 90% for >5m, we should spin up burst pool. runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/burst-capacity

Maya K.: note for primary/secondary: i'll be primary until 04:00 UTC, Priya is secondary for 15m then Evan will be secondary if Priya needs to handoff. please update the oncall board. 

Priya D.: updated rota. added quick links to the thread: runbook (latency-regression), burst-capacity, kv-cache-fallback.

SRE Bot: pinned runbook links to thread and added retention tag `oncall-handoff`.

Maya K.: quick remediation cheatsheet (put in this thread for whoever picks up next):
- check IncidentBot summary first (pager reason + sev)
- validate customer impact via support dashboard (Support->Active Tickets)
- run KV cache query and GPU util commands (links above)
- if hit-rate drop: emergency config patch (link) or rollback if config patch fails
- if host saturation: scale burst pool or enable fallback routing
- notify support + account managers if timeouts >1% for >10m

Evan S.: adding final note: when doing emergency config patches, use `--dry-run` on staging, then `apply` to prod, and monitor `rwdctl events` for rejections.

Maya K.: thanks all. i'll keep monitoring for 15m then update last_message_ts and mark this resolved in IncidentBot if stable. :thumbsup:

(10m later)

Maya K.: p95 stable at 1.25s for 12m, SSO timeouts back to normal. marking as monitored; leaving primary until 04:00 UTC. closing thread in 30m if no regressions.

IncidentBot: [CLOSE-PENDING] latency-regression-us-west-2 — monitoring OK, will auto-close in 30m if metrics stable.

Priya D.: thanks for clean handoff and the checklist — super helpful.

Maya K.: good handoff. tagging this thread for runbook examples and adding the `handoff/latency` tag on the incident page.

(End of thread)
